messages:
oliver: quick proposal — we should add a lightweight "offset-repair" handshake for streaming responses so clients can tell the edge what token-index they last saw. goal: allow safe resume without replaying user-visible tokens or recharging customers for duplicates. idea sketch below.

maria: curious — is this just a nicer resume token or are we exposing absolute offsets? any perf/consistency tradeoffs?

raj: caution: resume semantics can interact badly with side effects (webhooks, DB writes). if we re-run the model we might retrigger effects. need strict rules about when a resume is allowed vs when we must fall back to a cold call.

oliver: agreed. plan is: clients send X-Stream-Resume-Offset header with last-seen token index. edge verifies against an ephemeral checkpoint mapping (lease-based). if offset matches within epsilon window -> resume from KV cache; else -> abort-to-fresh request. keep resume disabled for requests flagged as "side-effectful".

sylvia: proposed wire example:
```
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer ...
  X-Stream-Resume-Offset: 1243
  X-Stream-Checkpoint-ID: kvc-9a2f
  X-Idempotency-Key: client-call-123
Body: { prompt: ... , flags: { allow_resume: true } }
```
Edge behavior: lookup checkpoint kvc-9a2f (soft-state), validate token 1243 against stored checkpoint range, verify idempotency-key. if in-range -> attach resume context to request router; else -> reject with 409/resume-needed.

sam: billing note: we must avoid charging twice. either we: 1) don't bill resumed tokens (edge dedupes by checkpoint), or 2) bill full stream but credit duplicates later. option 1 is preferable but requires us to persist per-checkpoint billed-token-count briefly. storage + ops cost = tradeoff.

raj: about budgets: we should gate resumes by a per-tenant "graceful-retry-budget" (tokens allowed for repair/resume per minute). prevents abuse or accidental infinite resume loops. implement as token-bucket on ingress, tracked by tenant-id.

oliver: good. eviction/TTL plan: keep checkpoints in ingress memory for N seconds (configurable) with lease refresh on successful streaming heartbeats. after TTL they expire and resume fails fast. avoids long-lived memory retention.

sam: config sketch (ingress):
```yaml
resume_window_tokens: 2048   # max gap allowed to resume
checkpoint_ttl_seconds: 90  # lease length for checkpoint state
resume_budget_per_minute: 5000  # tokens allowed for resume repairs per tenant
side_effect_flags: ["webhook", "payment"]  # never resume these
```

maria: operational/observability: emit metrics "stream.resume.attempts", "stream.resume.success", "stream.offset.gap", "stream.resume.billed_tokens_credited" and traces that include checkpoint-id and offset. expose in Console per-tenant so customers can see resume hit-rate.

raj: implementation caveats: 1) KV cache needs to be stable across short edge restarts (or checkpoint validity will drop), 2) need clear TTL semantics to avoid inconsistent resume, 3) ensure we don't leak sensitive prompt context in shared logs.

sylvia: security: checkpoint id should be unguessable (HMAC'd with tenant secret) and include a short expiry. also require that checkpoint is bound to idempotency-key and client-ip (optional) to reduce token theft risk.

oliver: sounds like a path forward. next step: draft RFC with state machine (REQUESTED -> CHECKPOINT_LOOKUP -> RESUME_OK / RESUME_REJECT -> FALLBACK). owners: @sam to draft, @sylvia for security review, @raj for side-effect rules.

sam: I'll take the RFC. will sketch state machine + perf numbers for a small-scale prototype. :+1:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: short-lived feature branch CI job queued for "stream-offset-resume-prototype" (job 4827).

maria: tiny UX ask — include human-readable resume rejection codes (e.g., EXPIRED_CHECKPOINT, OFFSET_TOO_FAR, SIDE_EFFECT_FORBIDDEN) so clients can decide whether to retry or show a fallback message.

oliver: perfect. thanks everyone — moving to RFC channel today.
